headline: This law extends the Federal Election Commission's power to fine campaign violators using a published penalty schedule through 2018 and covers certain disclosure violations.
what_it_does: The Federal Election Campaign Act lets the Federal Election Commission (FEC) impose civil money penalties, which are fines, for certain violations. This law extends that fining power, based on a schedule of penalties the FEC has set and published, through December 31, 2018. It also applies these penalties to violations of certain campaign contribution and spending disclosure rules.

who_it_affects.how: They can face FEC fines for violating the covered contribution and expenditure disclosure requirements.

who_it_affects.group: Political committees and other filers subject to FEC disclosure rules
who_it_affects.how: They must follow the covered reporting rules or risk fines under the published penalty schedule.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 26, 2013; the penalty authority runs through December 31, 2018.
